newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Iraq tensions, rate fears pull down Manila stocks.
newsitem.headline: Iraq tensions, rate fears pull down Manila stocks.

text.p: Manila stocks ended in negative territory on Wednesday as foreign investors stayed out of the market on fears of a U.S. rate hike and rising tensions over Iraq, traders said.

The main index fell 10.29 points to close at 3,197.60 following a 41.50 drop on Tuesday. "Worries over the U.S. rate hike and the Iraq skirmish dealt the market a double whammy," said Harry Liu at Summit Securities.
Brokers said trading was moderate with some 1.7 billion pesos worth of shares changing hands.
Losers swamped gainers 73 to 27 out of 177 issues traded.
Brokers said they see the market moving sideways for the rest of the week as investors wait for clearer direction on where U.S. rates, and world oil prices are heading in next few days.
The release of domestic August inflation figures on Thursday may provide some buying incentives as they are expected to show a continued downtrend but U.S. rates and Iraq will cap any rally.
